headline: Patriots season hanging by a thread after Drake Maye injury
morning_brew: I haven't felt this sick to my stomach since the T broke down on the Pike at rush hour. Drake Maye's ankle injury is just a total gut punch, and I spent half the night staring at the ceiling wondering if our season just went up in smoke. If Maye has to miss extended time, the offense is gonna look like a different animal with Tommy DeVito under center, and frankly, I do not have a great feeling about our chances against the rest of this schedule. It feels like we finally had a real direction with Maye at the helm, and now we are staring down the barrel of a complete rebuild of the game plan on the fly.

This is exactly the kind of disaster that feels way too familiar for a team that has been fighting to stay above .500 all year. We are sitting at 5-5 and right in the middle of a logjam in the AFC, and you cannot afford to lose your signal-caller when every single game is a must-win to keep our postseason hopes alive. My neighbor Rick is already spiraling about the offensive line and whether anyone can protect the pocket, and for once, I really cannot blame the guy for being concerned because his conspiracy board is starting to look like a documentary.

Looking ahead to the weekend, it is a busy Saturday in the Hub with two games on the docket. The Bruins are back at TD Garden tonight to face the Capitals at 7:00 PM ET, and I am praying for a clean, disciplined game that keeps the blood pressure manageable. Later on, the Celtics hit the road to take on the Kings at the Golden 1 Center at 10:00 PM ET, and I will be staying up to watch Jayson Tatum and the squad try to bounce back from that rough one against Denver.

news_digest.headline: Drake Maye ankle injury: Is the Patriots' season over? Can Tommy DeVito step up?
news_digest.dans_take: If Maye is down, we have to hope DeVito can manage the game and keep us from sliding into the abyss.
